candidates.changed_node: DIVIDE(TS_SUM($return,10), (($high-$low)+1e-8)) replaces A's dollar-volume-normalized range and B's return-spread
candidates.rationale: Keeps ($high - $low) intact from A (3 nodes) and TS_SUM($return, 10) intact from B (3 nodes). Fusion: instead of A's dollar-volume illiquidity normalizer, the raw daily range is used to scale B's short-return leg, producing a range-efficiency momentum (how large the 10-day move is relative to typical daily range) that is then interacted with B's ROE quality filter. Neither the pure range/illiquidity measure (A) nor the return-spread-times-quality factor (B) expresses 'move size per unit of range.'

candidates.changed_node: CS_ZSCORE(DIVIDE(TS_SUM($return,42), TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21)+1e-8)) is a new liquidity-scaled-momentum term
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_SUM($return, 42) intact from A (3 nodes, the long leg of the spread) and TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) intact from B (3 nodes). Fusion: the long-window cumulative return is scaled by average dollar liquidity into a turnover-adjusted momentum z-score, then interacted multiplicatively with earnings-yield rank. Captures whether a stock's longer trend occurred on relatively thin or heavy liquidity, filtered by cheapness -- a signal absent from A's plain spread-times-ROE and B's static earnings-minus-liquidity factor.

candidates.changed_node: MULTIPLY($earnings_per_share, TS_SUM($return,10)) forms a new numerator feeding B's liquidity denominator
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) intact from A (3 nodes) and TS_SUM($return, 10) intact from B (3 nodes, the short leg this time to diversify from the sibling pair). Fusion: earnings-per-share is boosted by very recent momentum and deflated by trading liquidity, then the whole liquidity-adjusted earnings-momentum score is filtered by ROE quality. A has no momentum or quality term; B has no earnings or liquidity term, so the joint 'cheap, illiquid-relative, quality name that is also popping' condition is new.

candidates.changed_node: ADD(CS_RANK(TS_SUM($return,10)), CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($close,2))) blends the two momentum horizons
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_SUM($return, 10) intact from A (3 nodes, short leg of the spread) and TS_DELTA($close, 2) intact from B (3 nodes, taken bare without B's SIGN wrapper). Fusion: medium-term return and very recent (2-day) price acceleration are each rank-normalized then summed (scale-free), so the factor rewards stocks building medium-term momentum that is also accelerating right now, filtered by ROE. A has no short-term acceleration signal and B has no medium-term magnitude or quality dimension.

candidates.changed_node: SUBTRACT($roe, TS_MEAN($return,21)) ranked as one spread, multiplied by A's short-term delta rank
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_DELTA($close, 2) intact from A (3 nodes, stripped of A's SIGN wrapper to avoid duplicating A's exact subtree) and TS_MEAN($return, 21) intact from B (3 nodes). Fusion: B's quality-vs-trend divergence is reframed as a single ranked spread (roe minus mean-return, ranked once, preserving relative magnitude instead of B's rank-then-difference) and multiplied by the rank of very recent price acceleration from A -- a timing overlay flagging quality-over-trend names just as they pop. B alone has no short-term trigger; A alone has no earnings/quality axis.

candidates.changed_node: SUBTRACT($close, TS_MIN($low,21)) turns B's value-ratio denominator into a new support-distance term
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_MEAN($return, 21) intact from A (3 nodes) and TS_MIN($low, 21) intact from B (3 nodes, repurposed from B's guarded value-ratio denominator into a plain support anchor). Fusion: multiplies the quality-vs-trend divergence (A) by price strength above the 21-day low (B, now a distance-from-support measure rather than a division denominator) -- rewarding quality names that have not over-extended on trend AND are trading well clear of recent support, a joint condition neither parent expresses alone.

candidates.changed_node: MULTIPLY(CS_RANK(TS_MEAN($return,10)), CS_RANK($high-$close)) is the new interaction, replacing both parents' normalizers
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_MEAN($return, 10) intact from A (3 nodes) and ($high - $close) intact from B (3 nodes, detached from B's TS_STD(high-low) volatility normalizer). Fusion: recent momentum is interacted with intraday closing weakness (how far the close sits below the day's high) -- flagging trending stocks that are nonetheless closing weak relative to their highs, a distribution-style signal. A's value-momentum spread has no intraday information and B's range-normalized wick measure has no return/momentum information.

candidates.changed_node: DIVIDE(SUBTRACT($close,TS_MIN($low,21)), ADD(SUBTRACT($high,$low),1e-8)) is the new guarded positioning ratio
candidates.rationale: Keeps TS_MIN($low, 21) intact from A (3 nodes, repurposed as a support anchor rather than A's value-ratio denominator) and ($high - $low) intact from B (3 nodes, repurposed as today's volatility normalizer rather than being divided by dollar volume as in B). Fusion: a stochastic-oscillator-style measure of where the close sits above its 21-day low, scaled by today's trading range -- range-adjusted support positioning that neither A's earnings-to-support ratio nor B's illiquidity-range measure expresses.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
